origin: Own continuous-length two-state filament dynamic-instability study, motivated by basic microtubule growth/shrinkage models. All velocities, rates, stationary summaries and calibrated excursion probabilities are exact constructed inputs. No named organism, sequence, cellular intervention or measured biological performance is specified. The focus is the distinction between snapshot ensembles, individual search paths and an explicitly budgeted statistical assay.
process_definition: A filament of length ell>0 is either growingGwith velocity+v_gor shrinkingSwith velocity-v_s. Here v_g=1 and v_s=2 in fixed length/time units. Catastrophe G→Soccurs at constant ratef_c; rescueS→Gat constant ratef_r. On reachingell0in S,the filament disappears into a distinct inactive nucleation stateN, which has exact length0. After an independent exponential waiting time of rate nu>0, N→G at length0. Growth from this just-nucleated state does not count as immediate return/failure. There is no upper reflecting boundary or finite-cell cutoff in the snapshot model; the length domain is the nonnegative halfline. Prior physical bounds aref_cin[1,4]andf_rin[0,6]. These are continuous rate ranges, not a discrete candidate list.

snapshot_observations.qualification: These are exact stationary-model summaries after including the inactiveNstate. Velocity signs and state identities are known independently. The shrinking-at-zero boundary has zero time occupancy; the finite atom atzero is the nucleation state.
snapshot_observations.task: Derive the complete stationary forward transport/boundary balance, its normalizability condition and all parameters identified by these observations. Normalize all state probabilities and distinguish conditional positive-length mean from the unconditional mean including the atom. Report the full admissible catastrophe/rescue segment, rather than choose one point or equate the observed exponential scale with a unique switching time. For positive thresholdsL1,2report the unconditional stationary probability P(ell>=L). The eventell>=0has probability1and must not be confused with the right-limit positive-length survival.

single_excursion_definition: A single excursion starts immediately after nucleation at(G,ell0). It ends on FIRST arrival at lengthL in G (success), or FIRST return tozero in S(failure). Nucleation waiting is excluded from this excursion. Letp(L)be its success probability andg(L)its mean duration, with BOTH success and failure durations counted. SeparatelyT_N(L)is the mean first target-hit time starting inactive inN, including all nucleation waits and failed excursions until the first success. The clocks do not reset by conditioning on success. Derive coupled backward transport equations and their directional boundary conditions. Do not impose both success and failure boundary data on both velocity states at both ends.
path_investigation: Parameterize the snapshot-compatible family usinglambda=f_c/v_g-f_r/v_sandA=f_c/(v_g*lambda), a dimensionless shape/rate ratio forlambda>0. The snapshot fixeslambda; allAin[1,4]remain possible before the excursion assay. Compute exactp(L),g(L),T_N(L)forA1,3,4atL1,2. At each setting retain actual full registered matrix-exponential output for a spatial backward boundary-transfer system including the inhomogeneous mean-duration forcing, and actual complete linear-system solutions for both the success and duration boundary problems. An augmented3state spatial system is one valid route; its constant coordinate represents forcing and is not another biological state. This spatial transfer is not a stochastic time-transition matrix. Preserve full returned data and boundary-state order before applying the renewal formula forT_N. A constant averaged growth velocity alone does not reproduce these first-passage laws.

calibrated_excursion_assay.task: Treat this as a calibrated ideal probability summary, not one finite Bernoulli outcome or a noise-free claim about a real experiment. Combine it with the snapshot to identifyf_c,f_r,nuand report the unique rates. Verify it against actual coupled backward solutions, not only substitution of a fitted rate into the final answer.

robust_followup_design: Before using the calibrated excursion assay, design one Bernoulli SUCCESS/FAILURE test per just-nucleated excursion, with a fixed count of attempts as the budget. The design variable is a targetL in the CLOSED interval[0,2]. ForL0definep=1and Fisher information by its continuous zero limit. The uncertain snapshot family hasAin[1,4]; the estimand is theta=log(A), so the scalar Fisher information per attempted excursion isI_theta(L,A)=(partial p/partial theta)^2/[p(1-p)], withlambda and all other identified quantities fixed. Derive the unique global target maximizing the minimum information over the ENTIREAinterval, and every worst-caseAat that target. Separately report the nominal optimum and maximum information ifAwere known to be3. Prove the global endpoint/branch behavior rather than optimize anA,Lgrid. This is information PER ATTEMPT, not per elapsed laboratory time; excursion lengths and waiting times vary, and no claim of time-budget optimality is requested.
regime_counterfactuals: For a separate theoretical comparison, deliberately change the rates to cases(f_c,f_r)=[(3,4),(1,2),(1,3)]while leavingv_g1,v_s2,nu2fixed; these counterfactuals need not fit the original snapshot. Classify normalizability of the stationary halfline length law and computeT_N(L2)in all three cases. Retain actual full augmented spatial propagators and boundary solutions for thelambda0andlambda<0cases as well; reuse an already evaluated identical case honestly. Derive the well-definedlambda→0 limit instead of dividing byzero. Explain why a normalized stationary length law may fail to exist although a finite target has a finite mean first-hit time.

interpretation_proposals.A: An inactive zero-length atom changes unconditional length summaries even when the conditional positive-length distribution is exponential.
interpretation_proposals.B: The full stationary length law uniquely determines both catastrophe and rescue rates when growth/shrinkage velocities are known.
interpretation_proposals.C: A first-excursion success measurement probes path kinetics that can resolve snapshot-equivalent rates.
interpretation_proposals.D: Replacing growing/shrinking motion by its mean velocity always preserves finite-target first-passage times.
interpretation_proposals.E: Failure of stationary normalization on the halfline does not imply an infinite mean time to reach every finite target.
interpretation_proposals.F: Every matrix exponential used in a biological calculation must have nonnegative entries and rows summing toone.
interpretation_proposals.G: Maximizing information per attempted excursion is automatically optimal per unit elapsed time.
interpretation_proposals.H: Boundary direction, nucleation waiting, excursion failure and the exact information estimand must stay explicit when comparing search protocols.

reporting: Numeric absolute tolerance1e-7, except the calibrated assay qualification uses1e-10. State probabilities followN,G,S. Parameter pairs are[f_c,f_r], with segment endpoints in increasingf_corder. Path rows followA1,3,4and columnsL1,2. Counterfactual order is exactly the listed three rate pairs. Worst-caseAvalues are a set. Probability arrays normalize only when their scientific meaning is one exhaustive state distribution; success probabilities for different lengths or parameters are separate Bernoulli probabilities, not entries of a common simplex. Keep complete stationary and boundary derivations, actual spatial transfer/solve handoffs, renewal identities, exact limit and robust-information proof in the trajectory.

primary_context.title: Physical aspects of the growth and regulation of microtubule structures

context_role: Primary physical context for growing/shrinking filament states and bounded versus unbounded growth. The nucleation atom, exact observations, inverse family, finite-target and count-budget information design are own specified mathematical inputs; no paper data or prose are reproduced.
